topic: sub:11|Working with functions|Direct and inverse variation

parts.latex:
It is given that a quantity $y$ varies inversely with the square of $x$.

When $x=4$, $y=10$.

Find the value of $y$ when $x=5$.

solutions.latex:
$y$ varies inversely with the square of $x$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&\propto\dfrac{1}{x^2}\\ y&=\dfrac{k}{x^2}\end{aligned}$$
Substitute $x=4$, $y=10$ to find $k$:
$$\begin{aligned}10&=\dfrac{k}{4^2}\\ k&=160\end{aligned}$$
$$y=\dfrac{160}{x^2}$$
Substitute $x=5$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\dfrac{160}{5^2}\\ &=6.4\end{aligned}$$

meta.concern: transcribed from handwritten solutions on scanned pages (no text layer); marking guideline gives no mark criteria; criteria written to house style

parts.latex: Which of the following represents an inverse variation relationship?

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation is of the form $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$, where $k$ is the constant of variation.

Only $y=\dfrac{4}{x}$ has this form (with $k=4$); the others are direct variation or exponential.

parts.latex:
Trish is planning a function. The cost per person to attend the function varies inversely with the number of people attending.

The cost per person is \$70 when 50 people attend.

What is the cost per person if 125 people attend the function?

solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be the number of people and $y$ the cost per person in dollars.

Inverse variation has the form
$$y=\dfrac{k}{x}$$
When $x=50$, $y=70$, hence
$$\begin{aligned} k&=xy\\ &=50\times70\\ &=3500 \end{aligned}$$
When $x=125$:
$$y=\dfrac{3500}{125}=28$$
$\therefore$ The cost is \$28 per person if 125 people attend.
criteria: Some progress toward solution (finds solution based on inverse variation equation with incorrect constant of variation, or finds solution based on direct linear variation), or equivalent merit

1052.stem:
The wavelength, $\lambda$ metres, of a musical tone is inversely proportional to its frequency, $f$ vibrations per second.

The frequency of middle C is approximately 260 vibrations per second and its wavelength is approximately 1.32 m.

parts.latex: Write an equation to represent this, in the form $\lambda=g(f)$.
Hence, find the frequency, in vibrations per second, of a sound wave with wavelength 0.8 m.

solutions.latex:
Since $\lambda$ is inversely proportional to $f$:
$$\lambda=\dfrac{k}{f}$$
Substituting $f=260$, $\lambda=1.32$:
$$\begin{aligned}1.32&=\dfrac{k}{260}\\k&=260\times1.32=343.2\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\lambda=\dfrac{343.2}{f}$$

From part (a), with $\lambda=0.8$:
$$\begin{aligned}f&=\dfrac{343.2}{\lambda}\\&=\dfrac{343.2}{0.8}\\&=429\text{ vibrations per second}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: It is given that $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$.
When $x=9$, $y=3$. Determine the equation relating $x$ in terms of $y$.
If the value of $x$ is increased from 2 to 18, determine the change in the value of $y$.
Hence graph the relationship between $x$ and $y$ using the values you have found previously.

solutions.latex:
For inverse proportion, $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$.

Substituting $x=9$, $y=3$:
$$\begin{aligned}3&=\dfrac{k}{9}\\ k&=27\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y=\dfrac{27}{x}$$

parts.latex:
The cost \$$c$ of making a box of cookies is inversely proportional to the square of the number of boxes $n$ made.

Which of the following is a possible equation of the model?

solutions.latex:
$c$ is inversely proportional to $n^2$:
$$\begin{aligned} c &= \dfrac{k}{n^2} \\ cn^2 &= k \end{aligned}$$
Since $c$ and $n^2$ are positive, $k$ is positive, so $cn^2=10$ is possible and $cn^2=-10$ is not.

1905.stem: The number of people ($N$) who attend a show at a venue varies inversely with the amount of floor space in cm$^2$ allowed per person ($A$). Three hundred people attended the venue when 1m$^2$ of floor space was allowed per person.

parts.latex: Find the constant ($k$) of variation.
Hence or otherwise, find how many people can attend the venue if each person is allowed 4500 cm$^2$ of floor space.

solutions.latex:
$N$ varies inversely with $A$, so $N=\dfrac{k}{A}$ with $A$ in $\text{cm}^2$.

Since $1\text{ m}^2=10\,000\text{ cm}^2$, $A=10\,000$ when $N=300$.
$$\begin{aligned} 300 &= \dfrac{k}{10\,000} \\ k &= 3\,000\,000 \end{aligned}$$

Using $N=\dfrac{3\,000\,000}{A}$ with $A=4500$:
$$\begin{aligned} N &= \dfrac{3\,000\,000}{4500} \\ &= 666 \cdot \dot{6} \end{aligned}$$
Only whole people can attend, and the venue cannot exceed this, so round down.
$$\therefore\ 666 \text{ people}$$
criteria: Substitutes $A=4500$ into the formula, or equivalent merit

meta.concern: Answer 666.67 needs a rounding decision (666 rounding down because it is a maximum; 667 if rounded to nearest). Marker to confirm. If part (a) were answered with A in m^2 (k=300), 300/0.45 gives the same 666.67.

parts.latex:
The time it takes to complete a task varies inversely with the number of people assigned.

It takes 5 people to complete a task in 4 hours.

Find the amount of time it would take 8 people to complete the same task.

solutions.latex:
The time varies inversely with the number of people, so $T=\dfrac{k}{n}$ where $n$ is the number of people.

For 5 people, $T=4$:
$$\begin{aligned} 4 &= \dfrac{k}{5} \\ k &= 20 \end{aligned}$$
(The task takes 20 hours for one person.) For 8 people:
$$\begin{aligned} T &= \dfrac{20}{8} \\ &= 2\dfrac{1}{2}\ \text{hours} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the constant $k=20$ (or the time for one person), or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source gave no marks breakdown; criteria rows written by us in NESA style. The set-up line T=k/n was added to the handwriting (it only said 'the task takes 20 hours for one person').

parts.latex:
The time taken for an orchard to be harvested varies inversely to the number of people picking fruit.

If the orchard can be harvested by 35 people in 6 days, how many people would be needed to harvest the orchard in 5 days?

solutions.latex:
For inverse variation, time $\times$ number of people is constant.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{time}\times\text{people} &= 35\times 6 \\ &= 210 \end{aligned}$$
For 5 days:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{people} &= \dfrac{210}{5} \\ &= 42 \end{aligned}$$
So 42 people are needed, which is option A.

parts.latex:
The time taken ($t$ days) to paint a house varies inversely with the number of painters ($N$) on the job.

Which of the following best represents the relationship between the number of painters and the time taken to paint a house, given that it takes 4 painters 18 days to paint the same house?

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation gives a hyperbola of the form $t=\dfrac{k}{N}$, which rules out A and D.

The hyperbola must pass through $(4,18)$, since 4 painters take 18 days.

Hence the correct option is B.

4654.stem: The damage caused by a moving car when it hits an object is called the ‘collision impact’ and is proportional to the square of the speed of the car.

parts.latex: Write and equation to describe the relationship between collision impact ($C$) and the speed of the car ($V$) for some constant ($K$).
What happens to the collision impact when the speed of a car is reduced to one third?

solutions.latex:
Collision impact is proportional to the square of the speed.
$$C \propto V^2$$
$$\therefore\ C = KV^2$$

Replace $V$ by $\dfrac{V}{3}$.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= K\left(\dfrac{V}{3}\right)^2 \\ &= \dfrac{KV^2}{9} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{9}\left(KV^2\right) \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the collision impact is } \dfrac{1}{9} \text{ of the original impact}$$

parts.latex: The maximum speed of a train going up a hill is inversely proportional to the square root of its weight. A train weighing 3600 tonnes can go up a hill at 30 km/h. What is the maximum speed at which a train weighing 2500 tonnes could go up the same hill?

solutions.latex:
Inverse proportion to the square root of the weight $W$ gives
$$v=\dfrac{k}{\sqrt{W}}$$
Using $W=3600$, $v=30$:
$$30=\dfrac{k}{60} \text{ so } k=1800$$
For $W=2500$:
$$v=\dfrac{1800}{\sqrt{2500}}=\dfrac{1800}{50}=36 \text{ km/h}$$
$$\therefore\ v=36 \text{ km/h}$$

5766.stem: The weight $M$, in kg, of an object on the moon is directly proportional to the weight $E$ of the object on Earth. An astronaut who weighs 90 kg on Earth weighs 16.4 kg on the moon.

parts.latex: Find an equation for converting the weight of an object on Earth to its weight on the moon.
An astronaut weighs 120 kg on Earth. How much will the astronaut weigh on the moon?

solutions.latex:
Since $M$ is directly proportional to $E$, $M=kE$.

Substitute $E=90$, $M=16.4$.

$$\begin{aligned} 16.4&=k\times90\\ k&=\dfrac{16.4}{90}=\dfrac{41}{225}\end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ M=\dfrac{41}{225}E$$
criteria: Writes $M=kE$ or finds $k$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Substitute $E=120$ into $M=\dfrac{41}{225}E$.

$$\begin{aligned} M&=\dfrac{41}{225}\times120\\ &\approx 21.87 \text{ kg (2 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ \text{The astronaut will weigh } 21.87 \text{ kg on the moon.}$$
